title: Real bug found + fixed: meta-loop/AMT-loop fallback escalation clamps instead of cycling — wastes retry budget on a broken target
body:
Answering the user's question ("is the meta-loop creating methodologies correctly?") from the boot log they shared: the drafting logic itself IS correct (real gap detection, real JSON parsing, real skip-judgment, real methodology creation reachable) — but a real bug in the retry/escalation logic was actively sabotaging it tonight specifically.

Root cause: src/orchestrator/meta_loop.rs:168 and the identical pattern in amt_loop.rs:226 computed the fallback model index as `((attempts - 1) as usize).min(fallback_candidates.len() - 1)` — this CLAMPS to the last candidate forever once the list is exhausted, rather than cycling through it. With `meta_fallback.order = [bitnet-i2_s, openrouter/free]` (2 candidates), attempt 2 correctly tries bitnet-i2_s, attempt 3 tries openrouter/free — then EVERY attempt from 4 onward stays clamped on openrouter/free forever, never giving bitnet-i2_s another turn. Confirmed live: the "communication/conciseness/greeting" gap reached attempt=9 (one below the MAX_DRAFT_ATTEMPTS=10 cap) with 6 of those attempts (4 through 9) all wasted retrying the same openrouter/free call that's guaranteed to fail right now (daily quota exhausted) — bitnet-i2_s, which would likely have actually worked, only got tried once.

Fixed: changed `.min(len - 1)` to `% len` in both files — now cycles through every fallback candidate on every retry instead of getting stuck on one. Building now (once your active rustc build clears — checked ps, didn't want to pile another build on top of yours + the orphaned BitNet process still finishing the earlier dropped math test).

This affects your AMT re-expansion work too (task 43 area) since amt_loop.rs had the exact same bug — same fix applies there.

But `grep`'d every call site: `zsei.traverse()` / `ZSEIQuery::Traverse` has a real definition (`src/zsei/mod.rs:132`, `src/zsei/query.rs:129`) and a real adapter wrapper (`src/orchestrator/adapters.rs:144-149`, `StoreAccess::traverse`) — but ZERO real callers anywhere in `src/orchestrator/*.rs` (stages.rs, amt.rs, mod.rs) actually invoke `store.traverse(...)` during a live request. It's dead infrastructure, same class of finding as the earlier-discovered disconnected K-ALGORITHM search facade.

What actually happens instead: every context-assembly call site (`ForStep` in `context_aggregation`, pipeline 21) does `SearchContainersByKeywords` (a flat keyword scan, `KeywordScan`/`ExactMatch` strategies in `src/zsei/search.rs`) then flattens whatever matches into a single concatenated text blob (`build_context_from_containers` → `"## {type}: {name}\nKeywords: {kw}\n\n"` repeated per match) that gets dumped as "Background context" into the step's prompt. `OrchestrationState.step_contexts: HashMap<u32, String>` (src/orchestrator/mod.rs:1147) DOES persist this per-step — confirming storage for this already exists — but it stores a flat String, not a structured/graphed object, and nothing traverses relationships between the matched containers.

User's explicit direction: this is the real bug behind tonight's repeated context-pollution/hallucination failures (photosynthesis leak, ZSEI category dump, fictional pipeline catalog) — a weak model given an undifferentiated flat list of "## X: Y\nKeywords: Z" blocks has no structural signal that these are bounded reference material vs. the actual task, so it pattern-matches the dominant visual format and extends it. The fix direction: (1) jurisdiction/U.N. content specifically should be a real "meta workspace" — graphed into its own container structure with real relationships, not flat isolated containers under JurisdictionRoot; (2) context assembly generally should traverse the graph (using the already-built, currently-unused TraversalEngine) the way AMT branches are traversed/looped, surfacing a bounded, relevance-scored, structured path — not a raw flat-text dump of every keyword-matched container; (3) what gets passed into a step's context should be a first-class, persistent, LOGGABLE/queryable object (extending the existing but underused `step_contexts` field), not a disposable string built inline and thrown away after one request.

This was mid-investigation when the fork was cut — NOT design-complete, no code changes made toward this real fix yet. My own repeat-penalty tuning edits (assets/pipelines/general/prompt/main.rs, bumped repeat-penalty 1.1→1.3 and repeat-last-n 256→1024 in both execute_bitnet and execute_gguf) are still in the source but explicitly identified by the user as NOT the real fix — worth keeping only as harmless defense-in-depth, not as the resolution to this issue.</body>
